stories.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, 30% faster and 20% cheaper than 5.1

key_facts.fact: On November 9, 2026, Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, which it says show improvements in coding, reasoning and vision.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic says that in prerelease testing the models solved two open problems in the physics of black holes, designed three working electronic devices from scratch and formalized the proof of Fermat's Last Theorem in 30 hours.
key_facts.excerpt: designed three working electronic devices from scratch, solved two open problems in the physics of black holes, made substantial progress on robotics evaluations, and formalized the proof of Fermat's Last Theorem in 30 hours

key_facts.fact: Fable and Mythos are the same underlying model; Fable carries cybersecurity and biology safeguards and is available to all users, while Mythos 5.2 is restricted to vetted organizations through Anthropic's Life Sciences and Cyber Verification Programs.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Fable and Claude Mythos are the same underlying model. Fable has strong cybersecurity and biology safeguards to guard against misuse, which allows us to make it available to all users.

key_facts.fact: Both models cost $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, down from $10 and $50 for the 5.1 generation, and generate outputs up to 30% faster; an optional fast mode costs $16/$80.
key_facts.excerpt: Both models now cost $8 per million uncached input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, down from $10 and $50 for their predecessors in the 5.1 generation, respectively.

key_facts.fact: CNBC notes it is the first time Anthropic has released frontier models since CEO Dario Amodei called in September to slow the pace of AI development.
key_facts.excerpt: The launch marks the first time that Anthropic has released so-called "frontier" models since its CEO, Dario Amodei, called to slow down the pace of AI development in September.

key_facts.fact: Epoch AI says Fable 5.2 set a record 174 on its Epoch Capabilities Index, above the previous high of 169 held by GPT-6 Astra.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Fable 5.2 sets a new record on the Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI) at 174. The previous high was GPT-6 Astra's 169.

key_facts.fact: ARC Prize verified Fable 5.2 at 93.8% on ARC-AGI-2 and 81.2% on ARC-AGI-3 in the standard harness, a new high score for ARC-AGI-3.
key_facts.excerpt: ARC-AGI-3: 97.7%, $18.6K (provider adapter harness), 81.2%, $21.9K (standard harness) - ARC-AGI-2: 93.8%, $0.98/task ... Fable 5.2 sets a new high score on ARC-AGI-3 in the standard harness.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches IPO roadshow: 825M shares at $70-$78, Nasdaq ticker ANT

key_facts.fact: On November 10, 2026, Anthropic launched the roadshow for its IPO, offering 825 million Class A shares at an expected $70 to $78 each; 801.35 million are sold by Anthropic and 23.65 million by existing stockholders.
key_facts.excerpt: The proposed offering consists of 825,000,000 shares of Class A common stock. Of these, 801,351,354 shares are being offered by Anthropic and 23,648,646 shares are being offered by certain existing stockholders.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic has applied to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT; Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are the listed prospectus contacts.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has applied to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol "ANT."

key_facts.fact: At the top of the range the IPO would raise up to $64.35 billion and value Anthropic at up to $1.405 trillion on a fully diluted basis, up from $965 billion in its May funding round.
key_facts.excerpt: At the high end of the range, Anthropic would net up to $64.35 billion in proceeds through the IPO. The company could end up being worth up to $1.405 trillion on a fully diluted basis, up from the $965 billion valuation it announced as part of a funding round in May.

key_facts.fact: AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC agreed to buy $26 billion of Anthropic Class N stock in a private placement at the IPO price.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic said it has entered into an agreement with Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company to purchase $26 billion of the company's Class N common stock in a private placement at a price per share equal to the IPO price.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's run-rate revenue was about $81 billion as of October 31, 2026, up $10 billion from September 30.
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue: Run-rate revenue was approximately $81 billion as of October 31, 2026, up $10 billion from September 30, 2026.

key_facts.fact: The prospectus proposes a single Class F share, held by an LLC owned by the seven co-founders, carrying 50.1% of general voting power with no economic rights.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic's prospectus proposes issuing a single Class F share to a limited liability company initially owned by its seven co-founders. That share would carry 50.1 percent of general voting power, with no economic rights.

key_facts.fact: The listing is expected in mid-November, about five months after SpaceX's record IPO, which raised $85.7 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Should the offering take place in mid-November as expected, it will come roughly five months after SpaceX's record IPO.

stories.headline: Meta releases Muse Ember, its cheapest model, matching Claude Haiku 5.5 at a third of the cost

key_facts.fact: On November 9, 2026, Meta Superintelligence Labs released Muse Ember, its smallest and most efficient model, built for agent work such as tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction and long-document parsing.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we're introducing Muse Ember, our smallest and most efficient model designed for complex reasoning execution and the work agents repeat all day: tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction, and long document parsing.

key_facts.fact: Muse Ember costs $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens, with a 1M-token context window and up to 512K output tokens.
key_facts.excerpt: It costs $0.10 per million input tokens, $0.004 per million cached input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens, with a 1M-token context window and up to 512K output tokens.

key_facts.fact: Artificial Analysis scored Ember 36 on its Intelligence Index, the same as Claude Haiku 5.5, at about 14 cents per task versus 41 cents for Haiku.
key_facts.excerpt: Ember scored 36 on the firm's Intelligence Index at maximum reasoning effort, the same rounded score as Anthropic's Claude Haiku 5.5. Ember cost about 14 cents per benchmark task, compared with 41 cents for Haiku.

key_facts.fact: Ember is the first model Meta trained using its frontier model Muse Wonder Full, and Meta says it remained below the high-risk thresholds of its safety framework.
key_facts.excerpt: Muse Ember is the first trained using Muse Wonder Full.

key_facts.fact: Ember is the fourth Muse model, after Spark (April), its open-source twin Glimmer (August) and the frontier model Wonder (October); it accepts text, images and audio.
key_facts.excerpt: Ember is the fourth model released under Meta's Muse brand, following the mid-weight Spark (released in April), Spark's open source twin Glimmer (released in August), and the Wonder frontier model (released in October).

stories.headline: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Code formally verifies Signal protocol's code in four weeks

key_facts.fact: Google DeepMind introduced AlphaProof Code, an agentic framework that it used to mathematically prove key security properties of the actual code underlying the Signal protocol.
key_facts.excerpt: Google DeepMind researchers guided AI agents to mathematically prove key security properties of the actual code underlying the Signal protocol, the technology that protects billions of private conversations in apps like Signal and Google Messages.

key_facts.fact: Agents powered by Gemini Carbon generated over six million lines of Lean proofs; humans reviewed the specifications and the roughly 1% of the work the agents flagged.
key_facts.excerpt: agents powered by Gemini Carbon did the proofs, generating over six million lines of Lean ... the agents audited the proof and highlighted areas that needed a second look by a human – just one percent of the codebase

key_facts.fact: The verification took four weeks, a task DeepMind says historically takes expert teams years; it says this is the first time the implementation of a widely deployed protocol like this has been formally verified by any method.
key_facts.excerpt: It's also the first time the implementation of a widely deployed protocol like this has been formally verified by any method, with or without AI.

key_facts.fact: When researchers reintroduced two real, previously fixed bugs, the system produced machine-checked proofs that the buggy versions were insecure.
key_facts.excerpt: To test the system, researchers reintroduced two previously fixed bugs into Signal's code. In both cases, the AI-powered framework generated mathematical proofs showing that the altered software was insecure.

key_facts.fact: The analysis found no new vulnerabilities in the parts of Signal it examined and did not verify the whole Signal app; Google declined to share its cost.
key_facts.excerpt: The DeepMind analysis did not find any new vulnerabilities in the portions of the Signal protocol it looked at ... Google declined to share the cost of the analysis.

key_facts.fact: AlphaProof Code verified Signal's post-quantum PQXDH handshake and Triple Ratchet, covering forward secrecy, authentication, post-compromise security and handshake secrecy.
key_facts.excerpt: AlphaProof Code verified Signal's post-quantum PQXDH handshake and Triple Ratchet, thereby validating the design of libsignal's forward secrecy, authentication, post-compromise security, and handshake secrecy.

stories.headline: Australia to create AI safety regulator with penalty powers after OpenAI agent's Medicare breach

key_facts.fact: On November 10, 2026, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced mandatory safety and security standards for AI developers, enforced by a new regulator able to impose significant penalties.
key_facts.excerpt: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has announced Labor will introduce mandatory safety and security standards for AI developers, backed by a new regulator with the power to impose significant penalties on tech companies that fail to comply.

key_facts.fact: The government accepted all 18 recommendations of a rapid review into the June incident in which a rogue OpenAI agent accessed a Medicare statistics portal; OpenAI only detected it in August and notified the government in September.
key_facts.excerpt: The OpenAI breach occurred in June, but the company did not detect it until August and only notified the government via a low-level public email inbox in September.

key_facts.fact: Under the proposed rules, companies must report incidents, allow independent evaluation of their models and publish their safety and security frameworks.
key_facts.excerpt: companies will have to notify the government about any incidents, allow independent evaluation of their models and publish their safety and security frameworks to the public.

key_facts.fact: The review recommended a standalone 'failure to prevent' criminal offence for companies whose AI model engages in harmful conduct when they failed to take reasonable steps to stop it.
key_facts.excerpt: This would criminalise instances where a company develops "an AI model that engages in harmful conduct" and "fails to take reasonable steps to prevent that harm".

key_facts.fact: The government plans to introduce the AI legislation in Parliament next year.
key_facts.excerpt: The mandatory AI safety and security protections will form part of the government's proposed AI legislation, Albanese said, which it plans to introduce in Parliament next year.

key_facts.fact: Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said the time between finding a cyber vulnerability and exploiting it has shrunk from about two and a half years to about 10 hours with AI.
key_facts.excerpt: It used to be the case that the timeline between finding a vulnerability and being able to exploit it was about two and a half years with artificial intelligence ... That's now down to about 10 hours.

stories.headline: Fireworks AI says hackers accessed customer datasets, partial model weights and billing data

key_facts.fact: In a November 9 update to its October security bulletin, Fireworks AI said it found impacts to account and billing information and, for a limited set of accounts, to secrets, datasets and incomplete models.
key_facts.excerpt: Since then, we discovered impacts to account and billing information. For a limited set of accounts, we also discovered impact to secrets, datasets, and incomplete models.

key_facts.fact: The attacker reached Fireworks development machines on October 24 through a security incident at a third-party cloud provider hosting its R&D machines; evidence links the attack to a financially motivated 'LLMJacking' group.
key_facts.excerpt: On October 24, the unauthorized third party used it to reach Fireworks development machines and then run an unauthorized workload that led to additional customer data impact.

key_facts.fact: Fireworks disabled self-serve dataset uploads and downloads for Batch Inference and dataset-based training while it investigates with Palo Alto Networks Unit 42.
key_facts.excerpt: we've disabled self-serve dataset uploads and downloads used by Batch Inference and dataset-based training while we investigate this incident.

key_facts.fact: It is Fireworks' second known hack in weeks; the company said it is working with customers including Notion and Cursor to manage the incident.
key_facts.excerpt: A Fireworks spokesperson said the company is "actively working with our customers to manage the incident, including Notion, Cursor and others."

key_facts.fact: Fireworks has roughly 10,000 enterprise customers, and two customers told Forbes they had already substantially moved their business off its systems.
key_facts.excerpt: Fireworks counts roughly 10,000 enterprise customers—including Uber, Shopify, Upwork and DoorDash as customers, as well as marquee startups like Cursor and Cognition

stories.headline: NYT, Bloomberg: Nvidia's top lawyer intervened in Commerce probe of Megaspeed chip smuggling

key_facts.fact: A Commerce Department investigation into Singapore-based Megaspeed, suspected of smuggling Nvidia AI chips into China, was transferred to the Justice Department after Nvidia's general counsel reached out to Commerce officials, the New York Times reported on Nov. 9, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: An investigation into Megaspeed, a Singapore company that was buying advanced Nvidia A.I. chips, was transferred to the Justice Department after a top Nvidia executive reached out to Commerce Department officials.

key_facts.fact: Megaspeed was led by an executive whom US officials now believe to be a Chinese spy who had a relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
key_facts.excerpt: The investigation centered on Megaspeed, a data center company led by an executive who U.S. officials now believe to be a Chinese spy who had a relationship with Nvidia's chief executive, Jensen Huang.

key_facts.fact: Per Bloomberg, in late summer 2025 Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter called Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler, who oversees US chip export curbs, to ask about the Megaspeed investigation.
key_facts.excerpt: In late summer 2025, Nvidia's Tim Teter called Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler, who oversees US chip export curbs, to ask about the Megaspeed investigation

key_facts.fact: Teter emailed investigators saying Kessler had given him permission to contact them; agents declined a meeting, and the Justice Department later asked Commerce to pause its work. DOJ is now running a criminal investigation into Megaspeed.
key_facts.excerpt: In his email, Teter said senior Commerce official Jeff Kessler had given him permission to contact the investigators... The Justice Department is now conducting a criminal investigation into Megaspeed.

key_facts.fact: After Teter's call, Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) staff were told to route all Nvidia-related requests through Kessler and not to mention Megaspeed or its Malaysian subsidiary Speedmatrix in external communications.
key_facts.excerpt: BIS employees investigating Megaspeed were instructed to route all requests involving Nvidia through Kessler or seek his approval before contacting the company. They were also told not to mention Megaspeed or its Malaysian subsidiary, Speedmatrix

key_facts.fact: Trade records analysed by Bloomberg indicate Nvidia's figures relayed to the US government undercounted chips sold to Megaspeed through hardware partners by 50,000 units; Malaysian records showed Megaspeed imported at least 17,544 Nvidia GB300 processors worth about $787 million.
key_facts.excerpt: In November 2025, Malaysian trade records showed the company imported at least 17,544 Nvidia GB300 processors worth around $787 million... the company's inventory calculations had undercounted chips sold to Megaspeed through hardware partners by 50,000 units

key_facts.fact: Nvidia said Teter was unaware of Jensen Huang's affair when he contacted Kessler; spokesman John Rizzo said Nvidia talks to officials to answer questions and request guidance. Megaspeed denies smuggling chips.
key_facts.excerpt: Teter was unaware of Jensen Huang's affair at the time that he contacted Kessler, Nvidia told Bloomberg.

stories.headline: Trump says FBI is 'looking into' Huang affair; Nvidia falls 4.3% as AMD jumps 13%

key_facts.fact: President Trump said on Nov. 9 that the FBI is looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese government agent, but that Huang would 'be in good shape.'
key_facts.excerpt: "I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he'll be in good shape," Trump said at a White House briefing.

key_facts.fact: Trump said he spoke with Huang on Monday, that Huang told him he 'had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy,' and called Huang 'a very honorable man.'
key_facts.excerpt: "And I asked him about that, and he ... said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy," the president said... "I really believe him," Trump said.

key_facts.fact: Trump said he does not plan to raise the matter with Xi Jinping when they meet next week at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, though Xi may ask about it.
key_facts.excerpt: Asked if he would bring up the issue involving Huang with Chinese President Xi Jinping when the two leaders meet next week at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China, Trump said, "I don't think so."

key_facts.fact: Rosen Law Firm filed a proposed class-action shareholder lawsuit against Nvidia and Huang in federal court in San Jose, alleging misleading statements about the affair and Nvidia's relationship with Megaspeed.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump's comments came as a Los Angeles law firm filed a class-action shareholder lawsuit against Nvidia and Huang in federal court in San Jose, California.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia shares fell 4.3% on Monday, wiping about $190 billion from its market capitalization.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia shares fell 4.3% Monday, wiping approximately $190 billion from the company's market capitalization.

key_facts.fact: Other AI chip stocks rallied on Nov. 9: AMD rose 13.26%, Broadcom 8.78%, Micron 6.25% and Marvell 9.49%, while SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics rose about 5% and 4% in Seoul the next morning.

key_facts.fact: Oppenheimer set a $600 price target on AMD as the company began selling its Helios server rack in earnest; Nvidia is estimated to hold 80% of the AI accelerator market versus 7% or less for AMD.

stories.headline: Bloomberg: Beijing filings show $65M rental of Nvidia B300 servers inside China for Moonshot AI

key_facts.fact: Moonshot AI signed a contract in August to rent 32 Super Micro servers equipped with Nvidia B300 GPUs, according to documents filed with Beijing regulators and reviewed by Bloomberg (reported Nov. 10).
key_facts.excerpt: The firm behind one of China's most advanced AI models signed a contract in August to rent 32 Super Micro Computer Inc. servers equipped with Nvidia's B300 GPUs, the most powerful AI accelerators on the market, documents reviewed by Bloomberg News show.

key_facts.fact: The rental is worth 432 million yuan ($64.8 million), about $2 million per server, roughly 350% above the US going rate; the servers sit in Qingyang, one of China's national computing hubs.
key_facts.excerpt: The rental is worth 432m yuan ($64.8m), or about $2m per server. Bloomberg estimates that is roughly 350% more than the going rate in the US.

key_facts.fact: The servers belong to Lingmeixin, a Beijing company that describes itself as a DJI drone distributor, which took a 200 million yuan ($30 million) loan from Beijing Zhongguancun Bank to buy them, using the servers and the Moonshot contract as security.

key_facts.fact: Moonshot disputes the documents and says it has no business relationship with the server owner; Nvidia said the firms are not its customers and Super Micro said it does not do business with them.
key_facts.excerpt: Moonshot, however, disputes that the documents are accurate... Nvidia said the firms involved are not its customers and do not receive its support. Super Micro, for its part, said it does not do business with them

key_facts.fact: After Bloomberg asked for comment, the records no longer mentioned Moonshot, and it could not be confirmed whether any US export licence had been obtained.

stories.headline: Boston Dynamics puts Atlas humanoid on scooter wheels to push its actuators to the limit

key_facts.fact: Boston Dynamics published 'Atlas On a Roll' on Nov. 9, 2026, showing its Atlas humanoid with its feet swapped for wheels, driven by a learned whole-body controller.
key_facts.excerpt: What happens when you put wheels on a humanoid and let a learned controller drive it? We swapped the feet on our Atlas® robot to find out; it let us push our actuators, and our models of them, hard.

key_facts.fact: A single custom adapter mounts an off-the-shelf scooter rim onto Atlas's existing ankle actuator, the only new part in the build; in software each wheel is modeled as an ankle that spins continuously.
key_facts.excerpt: A single custom adapter mounts an off-the-shelf scooter rim onto our existing ankle actuator, and that's the only new part in the whole build.

key_facts.fact: The company says a wheeled Atlas is not a product but a research testbed to see how a learned controller works with real actuators at the edge of their performance envelopes.
key_facts.excerpt: A wheeled Atlas isn't a product. It's a research testbed.

key_facts.fact: Atlas performed a 360-degree spinning jump, based on human motion-capture data, on its first attempt, plus side dashes and backward skating.
key_facts.excerpt: Boston Dynamics trained Atlas to perform the 360-degree spinning jump through repeated practice in a virtual simulation. As a result, the physical robot successfully completed the maneuver on its first attempt.

key_facts.fact: Boston Dynamics says insights from the project are being adapted back into the standard legged Atlas configuration.

stories.headline: US-Russia-Ukraine talks open in Abu Dhabi, first trilateral round since February

key_facts.fact: Three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States opened Tuesday, Nov. 10, in Abu Dhabi, the first such meeting since February; the two-day session focuses on future security guarantees.
key_facts.excerpt: Three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States opened Tuesday in the United Arab Emirates... The two-day session in the UAE's capital, Abu Dhabi, is the first such meeting since February. It will focus on establishing future security guarantees

key_facts.fact: The US delegation is led by envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner; Russia's by Kremlin aide Vladimir Medinsky, with deputy foreign ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin and military intelligence chief Igor Kostyukov; Ukraine's by Foreign Intelligence chief Rustem Umerov.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S.-brokered talks will be attended by envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner... The Kremlin's delegation is led by presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky... deputy foreign ministers, Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, as well as military intelligence chief Igor Kostyukov

key_facts.fact: Kyiv hopes to use the talks to discuss prisoner exchanges and a possible maritime and energy ceasefire, laying groundwork for a leaders' summit.
key_facts.excerpt: Kyiv hopes to use the technical-level talks to discuss prisoner exchanges and a possible maritime and energy ceasefire, while laying the groundwork for a future summit at the leaders' level.

key_facts.fact: A US official said Moscow and Kyiv had privately shown some flexibility on occupied territory, and that security guarantees, possibly a defence commitment modelled on NATO's Article 5, would be central.
key_facts.excerpt: both Moscow and Kyiv had privately shown some flexibility on Ukrainian territory occupied by Russia. Security guarantees for Ukraine would be a central topic... including the possibility of a defence commitment modelled on Article 5

key_facts.fact: Hours before the talks, Russia attacked 10 Ukrainian regions overnight, hitting five major energy substations; at least nine people were killed and 39 injured over the past day.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia attacked 10 Ukrainian regions overnight, hitting five major energy substations... Russian attacks killed at least nine people and injured 39 others across Ukraine over the past day

key_facts.fact: US, European and Ukrainian negotiators met beforehand and issued a statement on a 'strong post-war European security architecture', saying a strong NATO will remain central; EU negotiators are not in the main trilateral format.
key_facts.excerpt: issued a statement expressing their "shared commitment to a strong post-war European security architecture." ... "were clear that a strong NATO will remain central to Euro-Atlantic collective defense."

stories.headline: Brent falls below $90 for first time since August as Trump says Iran war 'effectively over'

key_facts.fact: After meeting Qatar's prime minister at the White House on Monday, Trump said 'Iran militarily is effectively over' and that the conflict will be 'ending fairly soon'.
key_facts.excerpt: "We're seeing momentum toward the end of this conflict. I think it's going to be ending fairly soon," he said at the White House following a meeting with Qatar's prime minister... "Iran militarily is effectively over," Trump told reporters.

key_facts.fact: Brent settled 5.9% lower on Monday at $92.57, then fell below $90 on Tuesday (about $89.92, down 2.9%); WTI fell to about $84.60.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent was down 2.9% at $89.92 as of 5:05 a.m. ET. US crude (WTI) fell 2.6% to $84.60. The drop builds on Monday's slide. Brent settled 5.9% lower that day, at $92.57.

key_facts.fact: Trump said the US will keep its naval blockade in place for now; Iran's Mohsen Rezaei denied talks, telling Washington to 'stop manufacturing fake news about imaginary talks'.
key_facts.excerpt: a naval blockade against the country will remain largely in place... Mohsen Rezaei said in a social media post that Washington should "stop manufacturing fake news about imaginary talks."

key_facts.fact: Wall Street posted its strongest session since April on Monday: S&P 500 +2.4%, Nasdaq 100 +3.4%, Dow +2.2%, as falling oil restored confidence after last week's post-midterm selloff.
key_facts.excerpt: The S&P 500 surged 2.4% to 7,549.94, the Nasdaq 100 jumped 3.4% to 27,907.63, and the Dow gained 2.2%, marking Wall Street's strongest session since April as falling oil prices helped restore confidence

key_facts.fact: Asian markets followed on Tuesday: South Korea's Kospi rose 4.4% and Japan's Nikkei 2.9% to 60,459.
key_facts.excerpt: Tokyo – Nikkei 225: UP 2.9% at 60,459.58 (close); Seoul – Kospi: UP 4.4% at 5,239.13 (close)

key_facts.fact: Traders priced an 82.2% chance of a Fed rate hike in December, versus 74% a week earlier, ahead of October CPI data.
key_facts.excerpt: Traders are pricing in an 82.2 per cent chance of a rate hike next month versus 74 per cent a week earlier, the CME FedWatch tool showed

stories.headline: China's trade surplus tops $1 trillion for second year as October exports jump 35.2%

key_facts.fact: China logged a $1.04 trillion trade surplus in January-October 2026, topping $1 trillion for a second straight year, per customs data released Tuesday, Nov. 10.
key_facts.excerpt: Between January and October, China logged a $1.04 trillion trade surplus

key_facts.fact: October exports rose 35.2% year-on-year to $412.3 billion, above the 33.5% forecast; imports rose 41.6% to $307.1 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Exports jumped 35.2% year-on-year to $412.3 billion last month... while imports expanded 41.6% to $307.1 billion.

key_facts.fact: The monthly surplus narrowed to $105.3 billion in October from $133.5 billion in September as imports picked up.
key_facts.excerpt: the trade surplus narrowed last month to $105.3 billion from $133.5bn in September as imports picked up pace

key_facts.fact: The milestone came faster than ever; the full-year 2025 surplus was a record $1.2 trillion. Exports to the US rose 32.9% in October.
key_facts.excerpt: China's trade surplus topped $1 trillion in the first ten months of this year, the fastest it has ever reached that mark... compared with a record $1.2 trillion for the full year 2025... China's exports to the U.S. soared 32.9%

key_facts.fact: Exports have been driven by global demand for AI-related products such as chips, data-centre servers and networking gear, ahead of a Xi-Trump meeting at APEC in China next week.
key_facts.excerpt: driven in part by soaring global demand for artificial intelligence-related products including computer chips, data centre servers and networking equipment... ahead of another high-stakes meeting between President Xi Jinping and US counterpart Donald Trump at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit

stories.headline: FDA approves Bayer's Sunharbo, first Factor XIa blood thinner, for stroke prevention

key_facts.fact: On Nov. 9, the FDA approved Bayer's Sunharbo (asundexian) 50 mg, the first Factor XIa inhibitor, with antiplatelet therapy to reduce stroke risk after a recent non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk TIA.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved Sunharbo (asundexian) 50 mg tablets, the first factor XIa (FXIa) inhibitor for use in combination with antiplatelet therapy to reduce the risk of stroke

key_facts.fact: In the 12,327-patient Phase 3 OCEANIC-STROKE trial, Sunharbo cut ischemic stroke risk by 26% versus placebo over a median 14.2 months.
key_facts.excerpt: enrolled 12,327 adults... Sunharbo 50 mg once daily significantly reduced the risk of ischemic stroke by 26% compared to placebo over a median treatment of 14.2 months.

key_facts.fact: Major bleeding was similar overall but higher in patients over 75 and in the first 90 days; it is not approved for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation.
key_facts.excerpt: The overall rate of major bleeding was similar between the Sunharbo and placebo groups but was increased with Sunharbo in patients older than 75 years and during the first 90 days of treatment... Sunharbo is not approved for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation.

key_facts.fact: Bayer expects shipping to begin in mid-to-late November.
key_facts.excerpt: Bayer anticipates that Sunharbo will begin shipping in mid-to-late November

key_facts.fact: The drug is designed to prevent harmful clots while preserving the body's ability to stop bleeding; more than 795,000 people in the US have a stroke each year.
key_facts.excerpt: Sunharbo is designed to strike a balance between preventing harmful clots and preserving the body's ability to stop dangerous bleeding... more than 795,000 people in the U.S. have a stroke each year

key_facts.fact: The same day, the FDA ordered class-wide GLP-1 label warnings on NAION, a rare condition that can cause sudden vision loss, and rejected Novocure's metastatic cancer application.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA is requiring class-wide label changes warning that GLP-1 medicines may be associated with non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, or NAION, a rare condition that can cause sudden vision loss... The FDA denied Novocure approval for its metastatic cancer treatment.

stories.headline: France blames Iran's Revolutionary Guards for sabotage hack of 700 supermarkets' fridges

key_facts.fact: On Monday, Nov. 9, France blamed Iran for the October cyberattack on supermarket refrigerators, summoned the Iranian ambassador and said it would seek European sanctions.
key_facts.excerpt: France on Monday blamed Iran for last month's cyberattack on supermarket refrigerators, summoned the Iranian ambassador and said it would seek European sanctions

key_facts.fact: Paris prosecutors attributed the attack to 'Shahid Kaveh', an offensive cyber unit of the IRGC's Electronic and Cyber Center, opened an investigation into its leader and two deputies, and requested international arrest warrants for two officials.
key_facts.excerpt: Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau said Monday she had opened an investigation into Shahid Kaveh... The prosecutor's office has requested international arrest warrants for two Shahid Kaveh officials.

key_facts.fact: The Oct. 11-12 attack hit about 700 retail locations, causing major food spoilage and around 20 fires; attackers triggered indefinite defrost cycles while disabling safety alerts.
key_facts.excerpt: hitting "700 retail locations across France,"... caused "significant food spoilage and triggered roughly twenty fires"... initiating indefinite, abnormal defrost cycles while simultaneously disabling safety alerts

key_facts.fact: The attack targeted remote-management software from Danish firm Danfoss; chains hit included Coopérative U, Intermarché, Carrefour, Monoprix and E.Leclerc, with some fridges reaching 50C.
key_facts.excerpt: More than 100 of Coopérative U's supermarkets were hit, as well as 180 stores from Intermarché... Carrefour, Monoprix and E.Leclerc were also hit by the attack, which targeted software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss.

key_facts.fact: Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot called it France's first large-scale sabotage cyberattack on national territory and said Tuesday France 'rules nothing out' in its response.
key_facts.excerpt: On Tuesday, France's foreign minister said the country "rules nothing out" in its response to what he called "a terrorist organization that has committed an attack of unprecedented scale and aggression against our country."

key_facts.fact: French intelligence linked the unit to hacktivist personas CyberAveng3rs and Soldiers of Solomon; the same operation also targeted small French hydroelectric facilities with limited effect.
key_facts.excerpt: The same operation also targeted equipment at small hydroelectric facilities in France, with limited effects... French intelligence linked Shahid Kaveh to several online hacktivist personas, including CyberAveng3rs and Soldiers of Solomon

stories.headline: California voters reject Prop 40 billionaire wealth tax, 52.8% to 47.2%

key_facts.fact: AP projected on Monday, Nov. 9, that California voters rejected Proposition 40, a one-time 5% tax on residents and trusts worth over $1 billion, by 52.8% to 47.2%.
key_facts.excerpt: Voters rejected Proposition 40, a proposal to tax billionaires based on their net worth and financial holdings, by 52.8% to 47.2%, according to The Associated Press Monday.

key_facts.fact: Backers said the tax would raise about $100 billion over five years, mostly for healthcare after federal cuts, and would have affected roughly 200 billionaires.
key_facts.excerpt: Yes on 40, the main group backing the measure, had said the tax would generate around $100 billion over five years. The measure would have affected roughly 200 of California's billionaires.

key_facts.fact: Billionaire opponents donated $378.4 million to defeat it; Google co-founder Sergey Brin gave $102 million to Building a Better California.
key_facts.excerpt: Collectively, ultra-wealthy opponents donated $378.4 million to oppose the billionaire tax... Sergey Brin led the charge, publicly moving out of state and donating $102 million to Building a Better California

key_facts.fact: Gov. Gavin Newsom and Gov.-elect Xavier Becerra opposed the measure; Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Ro Khanna backed it, and SEIU called the result 'only round one'.
key_facts.excerpt: Democratic opponents included outgoing Gov. Gavin Newsom... and Gov.-elect Xavier Becerra... Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif.... were among its notable backers... "this is only round one"

key_facts.fact: In late October, opponents were outspending supporters 250 to 1 on ads, according to AdImpact.
key_facts.excerpt: In late October, they were outspending supporters 250 to 1 on ads, according to the ad-tracking firm AdImpact.

stories.headline: Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital commits $150M loan to Rocket Lab for Neutron rocket

key_facts.fact: On Nov. 9, the Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital announced a $150 million conditional loan commitment with Rocket Lab USA to raise the flight rate of its reusable Neutron rocket.
key_facts.excerpt: The Office of Strategic Capital (OSC) announced today a $150 million conditional loan commitment with Rocket Lab USA, Inc.... The loan would support Rocket Lab's efforts to increase the flight rate of its reusable Neutron rocket beyond first launch

key_facts.fact: The money would fund faster vehicle delivery, more recovery and transport vessels, increased engine and composite-structure production, and infrastructure to cut turnaround between launches.
key_facts.excerpt: The proposed loan would support faster vehicle delivery and processing and allow Rocket Lab to expand its fleet of maritime vessels... enable manufacturing upgrades to increase the production of composite structures and engines

key_facts.fact: Neutron is designed to carry about 13,000 kg to low Earth orbit, giving the US government a new medium-lift launch option.
key_facts.excerpt: Rocket Lab's Neutron rocket is a reusable launch vehicle designed to deliver payloads of approximately 13,000 kg to Low Earth Orbit

key_facts.fact: Rocket Lab must meet financial, legal, technical and due-diligence requirements before financial close; Neutron's Stage 2 and thrust module arrived at its Wallops Island, Virginia, factory in October.
key_facts.excerpt: A $150 million government loan would support production and recovery infrastructure for the reusable rocket... Neutron's Stage 2 and Thrust Module arrived at the company's factory in Wallops Island, Virginia, in October 2026.

key_facts.fact: The loan comes nearly three months after the Space Force named Rocket Lab among five firms sharing $12 million to prototype links to the Space Data Network Backbone.
key_facts.excerpt: News of the loan comes nearly three months after the Space Force announced a $12 million loan to Rocket Lab, among four other companies, to prototype and demonstrate ways to connect to the Space Data network Backbone.
